title: Align bun.lock with package-lock.json
request: Work on the still open tasks: bun.lock vs package-lock.json sync

criteria.text: After the change, bun.lock resolves every direct dependency to the same version as package-lock.json (script: direct dependencies compared N, different 0; today 8 of 108 differ, 6 of them runtime: react, react-dom, @tanstack/react-query, framer-motion, lucide-react, react-window)
package-lock.json and package.json are byte-identical to before; bun install --frozen-lockfile succeeds on the new bun.lock
A bun-installed copy of the repo (frozen install in a scratch folder) builds with npm run build, the same way the deploy does
Six checks pass at the final commit; independent code review approves

notes.text: BLOCKED by the factory guard: bun.lock is in protectedPaths in .factory/config.json ('FACTORY GUARD: bun.lock is protected (artwork, secrets or history). Ask the human.'). Nothing was changed. Measured read-only before the block: bun frozen install passes, but 155 of 1023 top-level packages and 8 of 108 direct dependencies resolve to different versions in the two lock files (runtime: react 19.3.0 npm vs 19.3.1 bun, react-dom same, @tanstack/react-query 5.105.0 vs 5.104.5, framer-motion 14.7.1 vs 14.6.0, lucide-react 1.62.0 vs 1.61.0, react-window 2.5.1 vs 2.5.0). So CI tests one set and a frozen bun deploy would install another. Needs the owner's yes to touch bun.lock. Plan: delete bun.lock, run bun install --lockfile-only so bun migrates the versions from package-lock.json, then verify the 4 criteria.
